messages:
release-ops: Quick heads-up: we are instituting a temporary, targeted release freeze for the EU region following a KV cache spike impacting tail latency. This is a partial freeze — non-critical canaries and low-priority deploys should be paused for the next ~90 minutes while we stabilize.

alex: Understood. Which services are in scope?

release-ops: In-scope: any release with the 'eu' routing tag or that pins eu-prod model variants. Out-of-scope: infra-only config flips (unless they touch cache shard/placement). We'll post a follow-up list of active canaries shortly.

sarah: Are Dedicated customers (reserved capacity) affected? Do we need to notify accounts?

ops-oncall: Dedicated pools are not expected to be affected unless they rely on shared KV clusters; were running a targeted mitigation now. CS: we'll send a heads-up template to Account Execs after this thread.

tim: For teams that need to keep rolling, consider temporary routing overrides to NA or APAC. Example CLI we used for the Canary A/B reroute:

```
# shift traffic for service x to na region for 60m
redwoodctl routing override --service my-service --from-region eu --to-region na --duration 60m --reason "kv-cache-eu-spike"
```

maria: If a release is already in-progress (deploys started), what's the exception process?

release-ops: Exceptions: open a thread with "release-exception" tag in #eng-releases, ping @release-ops and the oncall. We will triage against these criteria: user-facing outage risk, security fix, legal compliance deadline. Expect a <15m turnaround for triage. See runbook: https://intranet.redwood/cg/runbooks/eu-cache-spike (internal link).

release-ops: Current actions: 1) scale read replicas for KV cluster (in progress), 2) pause low-priority canaries (done for known list), 3) enable temporary routing fallbacks, 4) monitor SLOs and report every 15m. Next update ~15m.

sarah: Thanks, will pause our non-blocking canaries and reroute the critical ones. Let us know when lift begins. :thumbsup:

release-ops: Copy. Lifting will be announced here once latency metrics normalize for 30m and KV queue depth is stable. If you see regressions, escalate to @ops-oncall immediately.

maria: Sent exception request for a hotfix. I'll post details in the exception thread.

release-ops: Received, team will triage. Thanks for the quick turnaround everyone.
